the section is present only when those conditions report an explicit True or False (Unknown is not a verdict and never reads as disconnected) and each field only when its own condition does; a disconnected agent or a False Ready condition adds a warning - the provisioning-derived status cannot see an agent outage), the provisioning.cattle.io Cluster's ready flag (derived from the Ready condition when present; falls back to status.ready) and conditions, its machine pools (name, machineConfigRef, quantity, roles), its members (ClusterRoleTemplateBindings with display names resolved from Users and UserAttributes, each row reporting principal, displayName, role, binding (the CRD object name), and system; a failed binding read omits the members field from JSON while the text card renders a members-unavailable marker, with a warning naming the cause; enrichment failure only drops display names, never rows; entries whose principal id is system-prefixed (Rancher's system principals, e.g. system://provisioning/...) carry system: true (Rancher-internal accounts, not operator grants)), its machines (CAPI Machine objects in fleet-default filtered by the cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name label; each entry reports name, phase, and the first failing condition message - preferring conditions whose reason contains "Error"; a failed LIST omits the machines field from JSON while the text card renders a machines-unavailable marker, with a warning naming the cause; absent when the provisioning cluster was not found), and the default registration token's node-join pair (nodeCommand/insecureNodeCommand), import pair (command/insecureCommand), and manifestUrl (on an imported cluster - provisioning spec.rkeConfig absent - notApplicable lists the node-join fields that are present but do not apply; fields are annotated, never dropped). The registration section is withheld by default because it embeds a live cluster join token (a credential that lets anyone add nodes to the cluster); pass --registration to fetch and show it. Sections degrade independently: provisioningNote marks a confirmed missing provisioning Cluster; an unavailable or ambiguous lookup and a failed registration read omit their sections with a warning naming the cause. Partial access degrades rather than fails: a collector this caller cannot read is named in data.degraded ({section, state, code, target}) with one paired warning each, and the command still exits 0. Cluster resolution and the management Cluster GET are required and hard-error. Degradable sections: provisioning (unavailable - the correlation, one entry covering the status, machinePools, and machines it leaves absent), machines (unavailable - a machine list that failed after a successful correlation), members (unavailable - the binding list; display-name enrichment failures stay advisory warnings), registration (unavailable - the token read).

commands.desc: Partial access degrades rather than fails: a collector this caller cannot read is named in data.degraded ({section, state, code, target}) with one paired warning each, and the command still exits 0. The user is required and hard-errors when unreadable; every other section degrades. The positional accepts a user id, username, displayName, or a fully qualified user principal (local://…, <provider>_user://…) - the principal form is the one way to name a user unambiguously when ids and display names collide. data.user carries identity (id, username, displayName, enabled, principals, created, system) plus everything Rancher records per user in UserAttributes: groups (memberships as last synced by Rancher, refreshed at login, a flat array of {principal, displayName, provider}), lastLogin, lastRefresh and needsRefresh (the group-sync cache's own state), disableAfter and deleteAfter (per-user inactivity overrides), and extra (per-provider audit extras, [provider][key] -> values; Rancher writes principalid and username today). All of them share one fate: when the UserAttributes read failed for any reason other than a verified absence (a user who has never logged in has none), every one is omitted from the wire - never an empty list - with the failure recorded in data.degraded; an omitted optional field on a healthy read simply is not set. data.roles.{global,clusters,projects} lists role bindings that EXIST for the user or any of their group principals. Roles are facts about bindings - never a computed statement of what the user can do (that is a permissions question, answered only by the server, and this command never asks it). Each row is the shared member shape (principal, displayName, role, binding, system); clusters and projects group rows by scope instance, with a best-effort displayName looked up per entry. Because the completeness of the role sections depends on the user's group principals, a failed groups read blocks all three too (their completeness would otherwise be unverifiable) - recorded in data.degraded alongside groups.

commands.desc: Prints a kubeconfig whose user entry runs the rancher exec-credential plugin. One context reaches the cluster through the Rancher proxy. When the cluster has the Authorized Cluster Endpoint enabled and the multi-cluster-management feature is on, the file also carries the direct contexts Rancher's own kubeconfig carries: <entry>-fqdn when the endpoint names an fqdn, else one <entry>-<node> per control-plane node, and the direct context is current. When those contexts cannot be derived (the endpoint's feature is off, the nodes cannot be read, no control-plane node has an address), the proxy-only file is printed and one notice on stderr says why.
